gates.text: Truth: no customer story, review, number, result, sender identity or deadline that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research. Gaps are marked [NEEDS FACT: ...].

Format: every email has a stated job, subject (30–50 characters), a preheader that adds information, a named sender, exactly one primary CTA, and a body of 50–150 words (up to ~200 for onboarding how-to); the sequence names its trigger, timing and exit on conversion.

Consent and compliance: audience is opted in or an existing-customer lawful basis is stated; no deceptive subjects (fake Re:/Fwd:, false urgency); one-click unsubscribe plus body link and a postal address are specified; auto-renewing trials get a pre-charge notice.

anchors.1: Same pitch repeated; no triggers or exits.
anchors.3: Varied topics on a fixed calendar; exit on conversion missing or vague.
anchors.5: Each email has a distinct job matched to the stage, behaviour triggers where relevant, branches on clicks, immediate exit on conversion and priority versus other flows.

anchors.3: Clear but flat; preheader repeats the subject.
anchors.5: Specific, honest and intriguing with the key noun first; preheader adds new information.

anchors.1: Corporate template, 'Dear Valued Customer', hype words.
anchors.3: Friendly but generic; no named person.
anchors.5: Reads like a note from a named person to one reader; first line about the reader; invites a reply where useful.

anchors.1: Several ideas and many links of equal weight.
anchors.3: One main idea but 2–3 competing CTAs.
anchors.5: One idea developed and one CTA with outcome-specific link text; any secondary point in a P.S.

anchors.1: Content ignores what the contact did or didn't do.
anchors.5: Uses known behaviour (what they signed up for, what they haven't done) and answers the objection most likely at that point, from VOC.

anchors.1: Image-heavy, link-heavy, spammy wording, no authentication or unsubscribe notes.
anchors.5: Plain-text-leaning, 1–3 links, alt text, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, one-click unsubscribe, complaint ceiling and sunset rule covered.

anchors.1: Open rate as the goal, or no metrics.
anchors.3: Clicks named but no per-email success measure.
anchors.5: Per-email job metric (clicks, replies, conversions), unsubscribe and complaint monitoring, and one meaningful test; opens explicitly excluded.
Concrete details from confirmed facts (times, prices, steps, names) in every email.
